passages.text: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke in a loud voice.
I heard Him clearly.
He called out to the executioners of the city.
He told them to come near.
Each executioner held a weapon of destruction in his hand.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנַ֗י ק֤וֹל גָּדוֹל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר קָרְב֖וּ פְּקֻדּ֣וֹת הָעִ֑יר וְאִ֛ישׁ כְּלִ֥י מַשְׁחֵת֖וֹ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And I saw six men coming from the direction of the Upper Gate, which faces north, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand. With them was another man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel saw six men.
These men came from the direction of the Upper Gate.
The Upper Gate faces north.
Each man carried a weapon for killing in his hand.
Another man was with them.
This man wore linen clothes.
He had a writing kit at his side.
All of them entered.
They stood beside the bronze altar.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה שִׁשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֡ים בָּאִ֣ים׀ מִדֶּרֶךְ־ שַׁ֨עַר הָעֶלְי֜וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ מָפְנֶ֣ה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְאִ֨ישׁ כְּלִ֤י מַפָּצוֹ֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וְאִישׁ־ אֶחָ֤ד בְּתוֹכָם֙ לָבֻ֣שׁ בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֶ֥סֶת הַסֹּפֵ֖ר בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ אֵ֖צֶל מִזְבַּ֥ח הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherubim, where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And He called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his side.
passages.sermon:
The glory of the God of Israel appeared.
God’s glory had been above the cherubim.
The cherubim were in the temple.
God’s glory rose up from above the cherubim.
God’s glory moved to the entrance of the temple.
God called to a man.
This man wore linen clothes.
This man had a writing kit at his side.
passages.original: וּכְב֣וֹד׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַעֲלָה֙ מֵעַ֤ל הַכְּרוּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה עָלָ֔יו אֶ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶל־ הָאִישׁ֙ הַלָּבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר קֶ֥סֶת הַסֹּפֵ֖ר בְּמָתְנָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: “Go throughout the city of Jerusalem,” said the LORD, “and put a mark on the foreheads of the men sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
He gave a command to the man clothed in linen.
This man had a writing kit at his side.
The LORD said, "Go through the city."
The city is Jerusalem.
Find the people who sigh and groan.
These people are upset about the evil things done in the city.
Put a mark on their foreheads.
This mark will show who they are.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלוֹ עֲבֹר֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֔יר בְּת֖וֹךְ יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהִתְוִ֨יתָ תָּ֜ו עַל־ מִצְח֣וֹת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַנֶּֽאֱנָחִים֙ וְהַנֶּ֣אֱנָקִ֔ים עַ֚ל כָּל־ הַתּ֣וֹעֵב֔וֹת הַֽנַּעֲשׂ֖וֹת בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone!
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the others.
He spoke so I could hear.
He said, “Go through the city.
Follow the man in linen.
Strike down the people.
Do not let your eyes show pity.
Do not have compassion on anyone.”
passages.original: וּלְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אָמַ֣ר בְּאָזְנַ֔י עִבְר֥וּ בָעִ֛יר אַחֲרָ֖יו וְהַכּ֑וּ עַל תָּחֹ֥ס עֵינֵיכֶם וְאַל־ תַּחְמֹֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Now begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the others.
God commanded them to kill many people in Jerusalem.
They must kill old men.
They must kill young men.
They must kill maidens.
They must kill children.
They must kill women.
They must destroy completely.
They must not go near anyone who has the mark on his forehead.
God told them to begin at His sanctuary.
They began with the elders who stood in front of the temple.
passages.original: זָקֵ֡ן בָּח֣וּר וּבְתוּלָה֩ וְטַ֨ף וְנָשִׁ֜ים תַּהַרְג֣וּ לְמַשְׁחִ֗ית וְעַל־ כָּל־ אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ עָלָ֤יו הַתָּו֙ אַל־ תִּגַּ֔שׁוּ וּמִמִּקְדָּשִׁ֖י תָּחֵ֑לּוּ וַיָּחֵ֙לּוּ֙ בָּאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הַזְּקֵנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: Then He told them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!” So they went out and began killing throughout the city.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the men.
He gave them a command.
He said, "Defile the temple."
He said, "Fill the temple courts with dead bodies."
He said, "Go out from here."
The men obeyed God.
They went out into the city.
They killed people throughout the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם טַמְּא֣וּ אֶת־ הַבַּ֗יִת וּמַלְא֧וּ אֶת־ הַחֲצֵר֛וֹת חֲלָלִ֖ים צֵ֑אוּ וְיָצְא֖וּ וְהִכּ֥וּ בָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: While they were killing, I was left alone. And I fell facedown and cried out, “Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?”
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet of God.
God sent judgment on Jerusalem because of great sin.
Men carried out the killing as God commanded.
While they were killing, I remained alone.
I fell facedown on the ground.
I cried out to the Lord God.
I said, “Oh, Lord God, will You destroy all the remnant of Israel when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem?”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהַכּוֹתָ֔ם וְנֵֽאשֲׁאַ֖ר אָ֑נִי וָאֶפְּלָ֨ה עַל־ פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֗ק וָֽאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הֲמַשְׁחִ֣ית אַתָּ֗ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּשָׁפְכְּךָ֥ אֶת־ חֲמָתְךָ֖ עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to me.
He said the people of Israel and Judah have sinned greatly.
Their iniquity is very great.
The land is full of bloodshed.
The city is full of evil and corruption.
The people say, “The LORD has left the land.”
They also say, “The LORD does not see.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י עֲוֺ֨ן בֵּֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וִֽיהוּדָה֙ גָּדוֹל֙ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ דָּמִ֔ים וְהָעִ֖יר מָלְאָ֣ה מֻטֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י אָמְר֗וּ עָזַ֤ב יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין יְהוָ֖ה רֹאֶֽה׃

passages.text: But as for Me, I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the people of Israel and Judah.
God said, “I will not show pity to them.
I will not spare them.
I will punish them for what they have done.
I will make their actions come back on their own heads.”
passages.original: וְגַ֨ם־ אֲנִ֔י לֹא־ תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל דַּרְכָּ֖ם בְּרֹאשָׁ֥ם נָתָֽתִּי׃

passages.text: Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reported back, “I have done as You commanded.”
passages.sermon:
A man wore linen clothes.
He had a writing kit at his side.
He came back and spoke.
He said, “I have done as You commanded.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֞ה הָאִ֣ישׁ׀ לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַקֶּ֙סֶת֙ בְּמָתְנָ֔יו מֵשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר עָשִׂ֕יתִי כַאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתָֽנִי׃ס
